These controls are complemented by international multilateral commitments like the Nuclear Suppliers Group and other export control regimes. These regimes maintain and update their guidelines and provide transparency and predictability to facilitate trade and build confidence among trading partners. These regimes provide an international benefit by identifying materials, equipment, and technologies that pose proliferation risks. They also promote standards and practices that facilitate responsible trade of those items. These regimes publicly release their technical control lists and transparently share best practices for assessing proliferation risk with members and non-members alike. The regimes are voluntary, non-binding, and respect national sovereignty. The control lists and guidelines for transferring sensitive materials, equipment, and technology are implemented on a national basis. Recent studies have shown that when both exporters and importers have strategic trade controls, dual-use sectors experience annual increased trade. Beyond helping states prevent proliferation and carry out their obligations under existing arms control treaties and UN Security Council Resolution 1540, strategic trade controls implementation facilitates high-tech global trade. and helps countries climb the industrial value chain and boost economic development.
